title: devbin ships docs treeindex, a command Intent v3 retired
body:
# 0032: devbin ships docs treeindex, a command Intent v3 retired

## Tags

catalogue, intent, v3, removal, fleet, dead-command

## Summary

hv retired `intent treeindex` from Intent v3 with no replacement (2026-08-25, relayed via intent/vc). v2 keeps it; v3 does not have it and is not getting it.

Devbin shipped `docs treeindex` as a **catalogue row** whose entire body was `intent treeindex "$d"`. So the day any estate moves to v3, devbin offers a command that lists cleanly, resolves cleanly, and can never succeed -- **the exact shape `check_commands` exists to refuse, pointed at devbin itself.**

It was not incidental coupling. `lib/cmd/docs` said so in its own header: "Both shipped options drive Intent, which is the methodology these projects share rather than an assumption devbin is making about anyone." Devbin owned the guard rails (refuse the project root, name an absent directory, capture the indexer's status); Intent did the work. When the work goes, the guard rails have nothing to guard.

## The blast radius is the fleet, not this repo

Devbin self-hosts (D12: `bin/.devbin/` here holds only `cmd/`, `config.yaml`, `help/` -- no vendored `lib/`). Every estate that installs devbin vendors `lib/builtins` and `lib/cmd/docs` wholesale, so every estate was carrying the dead row. Spot-checked three, each with the catalogue row and four call sites:

| estate    | `lib/builtins` | `lib/cmd/docs` |
| --------- | -------------- | -------------- |
| Intentv2  | 1              | 4              |
| Lamplight | 1              | 4              |
| Prolix    | 1              | 4              |

**Predicate, because it is part of the result:** `find ~/Devel/prj -maxdepth 4 -type d -path '*/bin/.devbin/lib'` returns 9. The established fleet count is 11 under *has a vendored runtime*, so that find is NARROWER than the fleet and 11 is not restated here as though it had been measured. They heal on the next re-vendor.

## What this repo already knew

`lib/cmd/docs` carried this comment, from issue 0016:

> measured under a v3 surface where `treeindex` is retired, both directories errored on screen and this function still returned 0 -- with an empty verdict artefact recording success.

So the v3 refusal had **already been observed through this very function**, and 0016 fixed the dropped exit status -- correctly, and without asking why the function was calling a command that no longer existed. A defect found while standing on a larger one.

## Resolution

Removed, not deprecated. A deprecation path buys nothing: there is no v3 replacement to migrate to, and a warning on a command that cannot work is worse than its absence.

| File                        | Change                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lib/builtins`              | the `docs.treeindex` catalogue row                                            |
| `lib/cmd/docs`              | `builtin_docs_treeindex()`; header rewritten to one option                    |
| `lib/config`                | the whole `docs)` schema branch -- it held only this key                      |
| `lib/config.reference.yaml` | the whole `docs:` block                                                       |
| `bin/devbin`                | the `DEVBIN_TREEINDEX_DIRS` export                                            |
| `docs/configuration.md`     | the `## docs` section                                                         |
| `.gitignore`                | the treeindex cache rule                                                      |
| `intent/.treeindex/`        | directory removed; `.treeindexignore` was TRACKED inside an ignored directory |
| `tests/unit/config.bats`    | the `docs.treeindex_dirs.0` assertion                                         |
| `tests/unit/docs.bats`      | five treeindex tests removed, two added -- see below                          |

`docs` now reports `usage: devbin docs <agents|all>`, and `docs treeindex` is refused at rc=1 with the usage line.

**Two tests were ADDED rather than only removed, because a removal nothing asserts is a removal that comes back:** one that `docs treeindex` is absent from what devbin OFFERS (not merely broken when called), and one that `docs.treeindex_dirs` is no longer a schema key -- a key the runtime stopped reading while the schema still accepted it is how a consumer keeps a dead setting for a year and is told nothing.

## Deliberately NOT changed

Named, because "we did not look" and "we looked and left it" must not be the same silence.

- **`AGENTS.md:75`** -- reads "in-essentials -- Core Intent workflow rules for steel threads, agents, treeindex, and session management". That is a **verbatim copy of the skill's own `description:` field**, reproduced by `intent agents sync`. Regenerating produces the identical line and would only churn the footer, which v2 stamps with a render date. It is fixed when the skill is fixed, upstream.
- **`intent/issues/CLOSED/**`, `intent/st/COMPLETED/**`, `intent/whiteboard/**`** -- the immutable record.
- **`intent/wip.md:30`, `intent/llm/LESSONS.md:48`** -- these record a MEASUREMENT that miscounted Riffle's generated `.treeindex` mirror as a devbin install. They are about a predicate that went wrong, not about the command as current practice, and rewriting them would falsify the record of how that measurement failed.

## The bigger half, which is not devbin's

**`/in-essentials` -- the skill EVERY session loads at startup -- still teaches `intent treeindex` as current practice**: 13 mentions, two numbered rules, worked examples labelled `GOOD:`. Found by intent/vc, who are routing the fix.

That is the class arriving in the one place no instrument points. Every discipline sharpened across issue 0031 assumes the agent's MEASUREMENTS are suspect and its PREMISES sound. This is a premise, stated by the tooling at maximum authority, wrong for a major version. This session loaded that skill at 07:18Z and was taught rules 3 and 4 as current; it did not bite only because nothing today needed a directory summary, not because anything checked.

A sweep that fixes only trees would report success having touched nothing that was wrong -- devbin's tree was the symptom and the skill is the source.

## Related

- 0016 -- measured the v3 refusal through this function and fixed the dropped status, not the call
- 0031 -- the instrument-discipline thread this surfaced during

## Resolutions

Removed in full from live code, config, docs, tests and ignore rules, with the removal asserted by two new tests. The upstream half (`/in-essentials`) is intent/vc's.
